unreproducibleReasons.foundation/time: Era pin needed, and the recorded pin is not it. The archaeology in sdkPinAtCommit resolves the super-repo gitlink AS OF THE ARTIFACT'S COMMIT DATE, which on a busy day is not the SDK the builder actually had linked: 2026-06-17 alone carries 20+ SDK commits. MEASURED at both b06faf5c (the recorded pin, SDK 0.8.4 / SDS 1.129.0) and aa5bf2e (the last commit of that day, SDK 0.8.4 / SDS 1.131.0) — both build cleanly from committed source and both DRIFT. The thread model is no longer the obstacle: these built at the current pin too (foundation/orbits excepted, below). Finding the exact pin is a bisect over a 20-commit interval crossed with two independent SDS roots, and belongs to modules-shipped-artifact-resign-wave.

unreproducibleReasons.analysis/lambert-izzo: Manifest-contract move blocks it at the CURRENT pin: its allowedTypes carry fileIdentifier "LMS"/"LMO" (3 bytes) and no rootTypeName, and the SDK now requires exactly four printable ASCII bytes plus a rootTypeName (invalid-file-identifier, missing-canonical-root-type-name). The oldest artifact in the repo (recorded pin 5a054283, 2026-05-05). The thread model is declared and is no longer the obstacle; the manifest is a contract change, not a reproducibility repair.
unreproducibleReasons.flows/supplemental-omm/nodes/*: NOT a thread-model problem — all seven declare, and their declarations agree with the shipped bytes. They shell out to a NATIVE flatc at <parent-of-repo>/flatbuffers/build/flatc, reached by a hard-coded ../../../../. repos/main-packages/flatbuffers is checked out but has NO build/ directory, so the binary does not exist on this machine at all and the build dies with ENOENT before it reaches a compiler. Of no recorded version even when present. Filed as modules-supplemental-omm-unpinned-native-flatc.
unreproducibleReasons.raw-emcc lane (14 modules): NOT a thread-model problem — all fourteen declare a THREAD_MODEL and assert it against the emitted wasm. They drive a vendored Emscripten directly, and the toolchain is NOT COMMITTED: only the emsdk bootstrap repo is tracked (137 files, no upstream/emscripten), so in a clean checkout build.mjs git-clones emsdk and runs `emsdk install 6.0.1` FROM THE NETWORK at build time. "6.0.1" pins emscripten but nothing records which emsdk build was fetched, and nothing records it in the artifact. Modules: analysis/{catalog-synthesis,od/fit-pipeline}, data-source/{bond-attestation-source,celestrak-supgp,cpf-source,glonass-source,gps-source,intelsat-source,iss-source,oneweb-source,spacex-starlink-source}, delivery/plugin-delivery, licensing/client-decrypt, flows/supplemental-omm/nodes/flatsql. Filed as modules-raw-emcc-lane-unpinned-toolchain.
unreproducibleReasons.data-source/iss-source (raw-em++ lane): MEASURED 2026-08-09 under the em-6.0.1 pin, from committed source at 17888ee, with no network access: rebuilt ee4bf0b757ef vs committed 332e3a3728c9 (62,969 B vs 61,542 B). The toolchain is NOT the cause and the section diff says so: type/import/function/table/memory/global/export/elem/datacount are byte-identical (29 types, 6 imports, 112 functions, 9 exports both sides) and code differs by 3 bytes in 56,304. The whole +1,424 B lives in the data section, in segments 3-5, which hold the embedded $PLG manifest. That manifest is encoded by the SDK, not by em++: the era manifest-exports.cpp committed alongside the artifact at 473162f3 declares plugin_get_manifest_flatbuffer_size() = 1,800, and encodePlgManifest at the current SDK (0.8.12) emits 3,232 — a +1,432 B growth that accounts for the +1,424 B observed to within array padding. So the raw-em++ lane has TWO build inputs, and this task pinned one of them: the compiler is now pinned and recorded, and the residual is SDK build-input version drift, the class already proven and recorded by modules-dist-not-reproducible-at-sdk-pin. Reproducing these bytes exactly needs the era SDK as well as the era compiler, which is the shipped-artifact re-sign wave's decision, not this one's.
unreproducibleReasons.analysis/dop: UNLOADABLE, not merely unreproducible. Its embedded $PLG manifest is in an encoding the current SDK decodes into GARBAGE, so assertArtifactRuntimeTarget refuses it on browser AND wasmedge and no current host will run it — verified on the bytes the live origin serves as well as on the committed ones. It cannot be repaired by a rebuild: analysis/dop is a build.js module and its build is refused at the current pin by MANIFEST VALIDATION before it reaches a compiler. Changing the manifest changes the embedded $PLG bytes, which is a Themis/Janus contract move. Filed as modules-plg-manifest-encoding-strands-live-artifacts.
